column2: With all four elements mastered, I must decide what kind of Avatar I will become. I can seek wisdom among the spirits, shape the world through diplomacy, wander among its people, or hone my martial skill to meet danger head-on.
Spend the year developing the path you have chosen as the Avatar.
Decide what kind of Avatar you will be: spiritual guide, political leader, wandering sage, or warrior.
A Moment to Follow My Path
My chosen path calls for attention. I should take time to strengthen the principles I chose to embody.
Guide the affairs of the world
The world is loud with fear and desire. I can quiet my mind and listen, or carry a little of that peace into the world.
Meditate until my thoughts grow still
Offer spiritual counsel to those in need
People look to the Avatar when rulers cannot agree. I can help them find common ground, or encourage the steady work of good governance.
The lives of ordinary people reveal truths that courts and temples often miss. I can help a struggling community or learn from those I meet.
Listen to travelers and learn from their stories
Skill fades without discipline. I can hone my own technique or share what I know with those willing to train.
Repeated effort has made my chosen path more than a title. Its lessons now shape the way I meet the world.
During a year of meditation, the boundary between the material world and the Spirit World seems unusually thin. I can listen carefully, or risk reaching too far.
A troubled pilgrim has come seeking wisdom. Their questions remind me that spiritual balance is practiced through compassion as much as solitude.
A dispute between powerful courtiers threatens to become a feud. I can settle it openly or risk myself by probing the intrigue behind it.
Several local rulers have asked for help coordinating their laws and duties. Careful diplomacy may prevent a future crisis.
A remote community has asked for help, but the route crosses territory where bandits and soldiers still roam. I can take the safer road or press on quickly.
Take the safer route and aid the village
Travel fast through the dangerous pass
A chance meeting with ordinary travelers offers a view of the world no court could provide. Their stories may prove as valuable as any formal lesson.
My training has reached a point where only the most demanding opponents can challenge me. A controlled lesson is safer, while a full-contact trial could end in disaster.
Experienced fighters have gathered to test their skills against mine. I can demonstrate technique without needless danger or turn the gathering into a fierce contest.
A Shrine in the Mountain Mist
I find a small shrine where villagers leave offerings for travelers. A quiet blessing may restore my resolve, while a deeper rite could bring me too close to an unseen presence.
A family believes an ancestor's spirit has become restless. I can help them make peace, or attempt a demanding ritual that could overwhelm me.
A young monk asks how to stay calm when the world seems unjust. Teaching them reminds me that wisdom is as much practice as knowledge.
During meditation, I glimpse a possible future, but visions are easy to mistake for certainty. I can reflect on it carefully or pursue the image with greater intensity.
Two villages argue over grain stores after a poor harvest. A fair settlement could calm the region, though one side may resent compromise.
Press the leaders into an agreement
A provincial governor asks for support against corrupt officials. I can insist on a public inquiry or quietly gather evidence first.
A modest reform would improve administration but anger influential families. I can build consensus or force the change through.
Rival envoys agree to meet discreetly. Their trust could avert conflict, but the secret meeting is vulnerable to discovery.
Take a personal risk to secure the accord
A flood has cut off a settlement. I can organize help from higher ground or cross a dangerous current to reach those stranded.
A healer traveling between villages has much to teach me about ordinary hardships. I can help distribute supplies or accompany them through a troubled region.
Travel with the healer through danger
A small town invites me to join its festival. Taking part may earn goodwill, while staying longer lets me hear concerns that rarely reach rulers.
Spend extra time meeting the townsfolk
Travelers report bandits in a mountain pass. I can warn others and take the long route, or try to draw the bandits away from a caravan.
A patrol is trapped beyond a damaged bridge. I can coordinate a careful evacuation or cross under pressure to help secure the far bank.
A respected master offers to test my technique. A controlled bout would still teach me much, while an unrestricted duel would be more dangerous.
A quarrel threatens to turn a training session into a real fight. I can calm the students or demonstrate how to disarm an aggressor.
A veteran points out a flaw in my defensive technique. I can practice it slowly or test the correction in a demanding live exercise.
Test it in a live exercise

Raiders flying no nation's banner have burned three villages in as many weeks, and the local garrison is outmatched. Survivors whisper that their leader duels anyone who challenges them, and has never lost. I can break the raids now, or track the war band to its stronghold and end this for good.
Break up the raids and scatter them

The trail ends in a box canyon: palisades, watchfires, and cages holding villagers taken for ransom. Their leader, a scarred earthbender the size of a badgermole, stands on the wall and laughs at my shadow. I could end this tonight, alone, or settle in and starve them out over weeks.
Settle in and starve them out

The warlord keeps their word: at dawn they wait in the canyon alone, while both our followers watch from the walls. Defeating them ends the raids in a single stroke, but they earned that reputation honestly, and one clean hit is all it takes.

Fishermen speak of a fog that rolled in a month ago and never left, and voices in it calling the dead by name. The oldest among them begs me not to go in after his son. I can ward the shoreline from safety, or walk into the fog myself and confront whatever wears those voices.
Perform the warding rite from the shore

Two blood-feuding lords have finally agreed to parley, and my steward has found poison in the wine, twice. If I leave, the talks collapse into war. If I stay through the feast, unguarded, the talks may hold... assuming the third attempt is not aimed at me.

A rockslide has trapped a caravan in a burning pass, and the wind is turning the whole valley into a furnace. I can organize bucket lines from the ridge, or go down into the smoke myself, where one wrong breath ends an Avatar.
Coordinate the rescue from the ridge
Go down into the smoke myself

A hermit sage, ninety years old and unbothered by all of it, has invited me to tea. The first cup is silence. By the second, I find myself confessing doubts I have told no one. There is wisdom here, if I have the patience to receive it.
Word that the Avatar holds court has emptied three villages: farmers with boundary stones, widows with debts, a tax collector with more seals than sense. It will take all day. It will be worth it.

On a forgotten stretch of road, a family tends a shrine to a spirit no one else remembers. They feed me, ask for nothing, and apologize for the meagerness of the meal. The least I can do is stop a while.
The garrison trains at dawn, and badly. Their captain is embarrassed to ask, but the stances are all wrong and the footwork worse. A week of mornings would make soldiers of them.

The world narrows to a single point of light. I have stood at the edge of death in a hundred lifetimes, and each time the cycle carried me on, but this time the wheel has stopped, and it is mine to turn. My companions are calling my name from somewhere very far away.
Refuse the void. The cycle will not take me yet
Let go, and let the next life begin
Set aside your current path and take up another. Anything you have already mastered stays mastered, but the rank you have reached on the path you leave is lost.
Seek the Counsel of the Departed
Enter the Spirit World where the veil is thin and speak with the Avatars who wore your face before you. Requires a devoted spiritual path.
Call the rulers of the world to a table that belongs to none of them. Requires a devoted political path.
Walk a road nobody maintains any more, to a temple nobody visits. Requires a devoted wandering path.
Summon every soldier of note to compete beneath the Avatar's eye. Requires a devoted martial path.
I have been one kind of Avatar long enough to know its limits, and my own. The other roads are still open to me, though whatever I have learned on this one will not walk them with me.

Something has settled in me. The stillness I once had to hunt for now arrives when I call, and the spirits answer more readily than they did a year ago. This is no longer a discipline I practise. It is becoming the shape of who I am.
Let the spirit deepen within me
Carry this stillness to the temples

The rulers who once humoured me now wait for my word before they move. I have learned which grievances are real and which are theatre, and when silence will do more than any decree. The world's politics no longer simply happen around me.
Let the world's affairs sharpen me

I have worn through another pair of boots this year, and the roads have begun to feel like home. People no longer bow when I arrive. They wave, and offer me a place by the fire. There is a kind of authority in being welcome everywhere.
Keep walking, and let the road teach me
Give what I have to every village I pass

The forms come without thought now. My body answers before my mind has finished naming the strike, and the soldiers who once watched me drill have started copying how I stand. Mastery, I am learning, is what is left when the thinking stops.
Drill the Avatar's guard in my methods

I have walked this road until it stopped being a road and became the ground beneath me. The sages would call it mastery. I am not certain that word means what they think it means, only that when I am still, the whole world is still with me.
Teach the stillness to those who come after

There is no dispute left in the world that does not sooner or later arrive at my door, and I have stopped resenting it. I know the shape of every quarrel now, and where each one really begins. That, it turns out, was the whole of the lesson.

I know the roads now the way a farmer knows his fields: where the floods come, which passes close in winter, which villages will feed a stranger without being asked. There is no map of this. I have simply become it.
Leave the knowledge behind for others

There is nothing left to be taught to me by anyone living. What I have now I cannot explain to a student, and I have stopped trying. They learn it by standing beside me long enough to catch it. That is how it was taught to me.
Stand as the Avatar of war
Raise up those who will come after

At the old shrine the veil thins to nothing, and the dead who wore my face before me are waiting. They do not speak in words. They offer me their memory instead: a lifetime of choices, and what each one cost. I can take what they offer, or ask them for something harder.
Ask them what I am afraid to know

Seven rulers send envoys to a hall that belongs to none of them. There is no throne here, only a long table and a great deal of suspicion. Someone must speak first, and every person in the room knows exactly who that should be.
Bind them to a common accord
Let them air every grievance before I speak

There is a temple at the end of a road nobody maintains any more, and the people along it have been waiting a long time for someone to walk it. I could go quietly, and arrive where I meant to, or I could go where the need is worst and never arrive at all.
Walk where the need is worst
Seek the temple at the road's end
The Avatar has called a tournament, and every soldier with a name worth having has come. They will remember who presided over it. They will remember far longer who won it.
